speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I recognise that businesses in the affected sectors have been working very hard to adapt to the changing regulations and are deeply disappointed by this turn of events.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last week, Minister Gan Kim Yong and I spoke with representatives from the Singapore Business Federation and several trade associations from the food and beverage (F&B) and retail sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also received feedback from several business owners.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many told us that their situation is more strained this time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just having to enter into another Heightened Alert.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is the broader challenge of having to endure more than one and a half years’ worth of restrictions, as well as continued disruptions to their business.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite this, they understood the need for the latest restrictions and have been appreciative of the support rendered.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have continued to show resilience and the resolve to ride out the storm.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economic agencies will continue to engage closely with businesses and workers and unions to hear their concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In response to the concerns and feedback of businesses, we are providing higher wage support this round to further mitigate the impact of protracted safe management restrictions and uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will benefit the F&B, sports, performing arts and arts education sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also enhanced support to 40%, up from 30% previously, for sectors that are significantly affected by the restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These include footfall-dependent sectors such as retail, museums, art galleries, historical sites, cinema operators, affected personal care services and family entertainment centres.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The tourism sector will also receive 40% support as their revenues are likely to be impacted by the restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will benefit attractions, hotels, cruise and regional ferry operators, meetings, incentives, conventions and exhibitions (MICE) organisers and travel agents.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Subject to the eventual situation, the JSS support will be tapered to 10% for two weeks as businesses reopen, from 19 to 31 August.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also help small and medium enterprises and eligible non-profit organisations with cash flow by providing relief for rental costs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do this through an additional four weeks of rental waiver for qualifying tenants of Government-owned commercial properties and an additional two weeks of rental relief cash payout for qualifying tenant-occupiers and owner-occupiers of privately-owned commercial properties under the Rental Support Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many commercial tenants have asked the Government to intervene and mandate their landlords to extend rental relief.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has set out the principles before.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our starting point is always the sanctity of contract; we do not lightly intervene.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we are prepared to intervene in specific situations and in a carefully scoped manner.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We decided to do so last year when we introduced emergency measures during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the last Heightened Alert, we did not require private landlords to extend rental relief.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we encouraged landlords to do their part to match the Government relief.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that not all landlords are in the same financial situation; some may have difficulty sharing the burden with their tenants.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, for landlords which are genuinely facing hardship, we will put in place a process to take their circumstances into consideration.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More details on this measure will be announced by MinLaw in due course.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To assist our hawkers impacted by the dine-in restrictions, we had earlier announced on 16 July an additional one month of rental waiver and subsidies for dishwashing and table-cleaning fees.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that our hawkers and market stallholders are affected disproportionately this time round, with many of them facing loss of earnings.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those operating in markets with active transmission have been required to close.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those who can operate have also been affected by reduced footfall due to public reservations about visiting markets and adjoining hawker centres.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why we have introduced a new Market and Hawker Centre Relief Fund, which provides a one-off cash assistance of $500 per stallholder who operates in Government hawker centres and markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To help our hawkers adapt to these disruptions, Enterprise Singapore will also reintroduce the Food Delivery Booster Package to help our hawkers defray the costs of using online food delivery platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will provide greater assistance to taxi and private hire car drivers under the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund from 22 July to 30 September 2021 in view of the anticipated drop in ridership.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also continue to help workers tide through this difficult period.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I had said previously that given the stronger position we are in today compared to last year and the fact that most of the economy remains open, we should not be drawing on past reserves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will therefore fund the support package through Budget reallocations, in keeping with our principles of fiscal responsibility and prudence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we have worked with agencies to identify $0.9 billion of one-off under-utilisation in operating and development expenditures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are due to delays brought about by COVID-19, so, they are one-off in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They include postponement and cancellation of activities in schools due to COVID-19 and construction project delays.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, these delayed expenditures will still need to be incurred in the future, once we recover from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, as part of the Supplementary Estimates I had presented in early July, we had provided a buffer of $0.2 billion in anticipation that this might be needed for modest enhancements or extension of the support measures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are now making use of the buffer for this package.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Supplementary Supply Bill which I am introducing today will reflect this reallocation together with that announced in my previous Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In all, we are providing more than $2 billion worth of support to workers and businesses over the two periods of Heightened Alert from May.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do not expect this latest period of Heightened Alert to derail our economic recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The domestic consumer-facing sectors like retail and F&B will continue to face challenges during this period.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as we continue with our reopening plans, demand should pick up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: About 70% of our economic activities are in outward-oriented sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We should remain on track to achieve GDP growth of 4% to 6% this year, so long as external demand remains healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The bigger uncertainty to our recovery therefore, is the impact that the Delta variant may have on the major economies in Europe and the US and on external demand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the whole, most economists are still projecting a robust global economic recovery this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are growing fears that as countries open up and the Delta variant spreads, the resurgence in cases could lead to higher hospitalisations and fatalities, especially among the unvaccinated populations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This in turn could force a return to lockdowns and impinge on global economic growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to monitor global developments, paying attention to any derailers which can affect us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To conclude, we must continue to stay agile and nimble and keep on updating our COVID-19 and economic strategies based on the latest developments around us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, the best way to support our businesses and workers is to bring the infection under control, push up our vaccine coverage and reopen our economy – all the things we talked about just now during the MTF Statements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, these continue to be our key priorities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to work hard across all fronts to help everyone tide through this Heightened Alert and to emerge stronger together.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Deputy Speaker, pursuant to Standing Order No 44, I beg to move, "That the Ministerial Statement made by me be considered by Parliament."

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Deputy Speaker, to give Members some time to consider my Statement, I would like to adjourn the debate.
